Version **0.2.2** replaces automatic and per-board library downloads with a manual **Download and merge** button. Each request downloads the full public archive from `https://stats.eternityathome.org/library/archive`. There are no downloads on startup, scheduled refreshes, or automatic retries. Old automatic-download settings are ignored; existing caches and search state are retained.

The archive is staged locally, validated, and merged atomically. Already cached arrangements are skipped, while existing cache entries and index metadata are preserved. Original archives and local backups are retained. Download and validation can take several minutes; progress is displayed, and cancellation is available until the final merge begins. Failed or cancelled imports leave the existing cache available. Closing the browser leaves a requested operation running while its local server remains open.

Only the manual archive operation contacts the fixed public library endpoint. **Search workers remain offline.** No discoveries, results, progress, node/work counts, or telemetry are uploaded. Normal server access logs can still record the GET request, IP address, and application's user-agent. **Export best board** continues to save validated files locally for manual review, with no automatic submission.

Duplicate lookups consult the shared SQLite cache, including newly merged arrangements. Historical “not found” results remain scoped to the snapshot at check time. A complete archive import does not establish complete coverage of the current public index or worldwide novelty. This release makes no claim of a better puzzle solution.

The search algorithms and measured results from v0.2.0 are unchanged. Choose pruned DFS, Glucose SAT, or OR-Tools CP-SAT in the dashboard. DFS uses color/rotation domains, adjacency propagation, piece uniqueness, and perfect-matching feasibility checks; its remaining search is checkpointed on Stop and resumed on Start. SAT and CP-SAT restart their native search on each start.

The bounded local comparison did not find a full 480/480 solution or establish a fastest full-puzzle algorithm. Pruned DFS is the fallback recommendation, with SAT and CP-SAT available for comparison. The portable DFS implementation is Python; its timings are not a benchmark of optimized native backtrackers. See docs/EXACT_SEARCH.md for tested scope and limits.

An experimental hybrid option first samples complete random legal boards on the GPU, including low-scoring arrangements, then freezes at most 64 validated candidates to guide CPU DFS ordering. Hints never eliminate valid search branches. Its measured sampling rate includes generation, scoring, selected transfers and CPU screening, but excludes compilation and initialization. It does not measure uniqueness or solution progress, and no solving speedup is established. Hybrid hints and checkpoints stay separate from plain DFS and GPU repair.

Exact modes target all 480 edges with all five official clues. DFS, SAT and CP-SAT use the CPU; hybrid adds the short GPU sampling stage described above. They retain the saved best board until an independently validated complete solution is found. Their branches/conflicts are local diagnostic counters, not production BOINC tickets, nodes, or credit. The existing GPU repair engines remain available through CUDA and OpenCL.

Opening the app starts its local dashboard; search requires Start, and an archive refresh requires **Download and merge**. Search and manual export work without downloading an archive. The project submission schema remains unconfirmed. Existing GPU checkpoints remain separate from the DFS checkpoint.

Native packages cover Windows x64, Linux x64, macOS Intel, and macOS Apple Silicon. Windows/Linux include CUDA and OpenCL; macOS uses OpenCL. Compatible hardware drivers are needed for GPU search. Every native package runs frozen exact-engine SAT/UNSAT diagnostics and resource/export checks. Linux additionally checks source and frozen OpenCL on PoCL's CPU device; these checks do not certify physical AMD, Intel, or Apple GPUs. macOS packages are not Apple-notarized.

No user checkpoints, downloaded library databases, local discoveries, logs, or credentials are packaged. Dependency versions, licenses and resource checksums accompany each archive. The BOINC CPU inspector and wrapper examples remain research tools, not approved production applications; the standalone exact mode does not reproduce or submit BOINC workunits.
